title: Logistic regression with L2, stable and from scratch
hints: np.exp(-z) overflows for z < -709. A sigmoid that never overflows uses e = np.exp(-np.abs(z)): for z >= 0 it is 1 / (1 + e), for z < 0 it is e / (1 + e). Or use 0.5 * (1 + np.tanh(z / 2)).
Do not compute log(p) and log(1 - p). The per-sample loss is softplus(z) - y * z where softplus(z) = log(1 + exp(z)) = np.logaddexp(0, z), which is stable for any z.
The gradient of the mean log-loss is X.T @ (p - y) / N for w and mean(p - y) for b, with p = sigmoid(X @ w + b). Add l2 * w (and nothing for b) for the penalty (l2 / 2) * ||w||^2.
